title: Cross-Layer Refusal Localization: Where in the Network Does Safety Live?

original_idea.body: Cross-Layer Refusal Localization. Problem: produce a per-layer map of where refusal becomes linearly decodable and whether it matches where attacks first disrupt it. Direction: train linear refusal probes at every layer of an open model, plot decodability vs depth, run a prefill/suffix attack and identify the layer where the refusal signal first collapses, compare across 2-3 models; activation extraction + sklearn only.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: per-layer refusal map informs which layer cheap monitors should read, connecting interpretability to attack dynamics.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Per-layer linear probes (activation extraction + sklearn); interpretability-adjacent, no training.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Open-model interpretability-adjacent work, no internal access needed.

low_compute.reasoning: Activation extraction + sklearn on open model, single GPU.

novelty.reasoning: Refusal localization (Arditi) and cheap probes published; per-layer decodability-vs-attack-collapse map may be open.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Refusal direction localization is published; the per-layer decodability-vs-attack-collapse mapping is plausibly open.
